title: Administration and inspection procedures of seed unit to ensure varietal pure seeds for certification

lessons.title: Running certification administration in the workplace
lessons.html:
Workplace scope

In this module you work in a certification office, seed company or inspection service, carrying out the administration and inspections that keep seed varietally pure from field to label. Over the placement you should handle at least one full season for a crop, from field entry to certification.

Administrative tasks to perform

  • Receive and check field entry applications: variety listed, correct parent seed class, parent labels and lot numbers, maps, area, previous cropping.
  • Capture applications in the register or database and allocate field numbers.
  • Plan and schedule inspections by crop, region and expected growth stage; allocate inspectors.
  • Issue inspection outcomes and conditions to growers; track re-inspections.
  • Match harvested seed intake at seed units to approved fields.
  • Match lots to sampling and laboratory results.
  • Control the issue of certification labels and seals for approved lots.
  • File reports so that any lot can be traced back to its field and parent seed.

Using the register

The certification register or database is the backbone of the system. Every entry must be complete and accurate. Errors such as a wrong lot number or variety name can invalidate certification or allow uncertified seed to be labelled. Double-check data capture, and reconcile regularly: approved fields against intake, intake against lots, lots against labels issued.

Deadlines and planning

Summer crops such as maize, sunflower and soybeans and winter crops such as wheat and barley follow different calendars. Build a seasonal plan so inspections happen at the right growth stage. A missed inspection window cannot be recovered.

Professional conduct

Inspectors and administrators must be independent. Declare any conflict of interest, such as a relative who grows seed, and do not accept gifts that could influence decisions.

lessons.title: Inspections and evidence of competence
lessons.html:
Field inspections in practice

With your mentor, and later independently where authorised, inspect seed crops at the prescribed stages:

  1. Confirm the field against the map and application.
  2. Check isolation against the scheme distances.
  3. Walk the prescribed pattern and make the required counts.
  4. Record off-types, other varieties, other crops, specified weeds and diseases.
  5. For hybrids, check detasseling or male sterility and pollen shed of female plants.
  6. Decide and record: approve, require roguing and re-inspection, downgrade or reject.
  7. Discuss findings with the grower on site and leave or send a copy of the report.

Seed unit inspections

  • Intake records match approved fields and harvest estimates.
  • Cleaning of combines, trucks and processing lines between lots, with records.
  • Clear lot identity on bins, bags and pallets at every stage.
  • Storage clean, dry, pest-controlled and segregated.
  • Labels and seals stored securely, counted and reconciled.

Safety

In the field: sun protection, water, sturdy footwear, awareness of snakes, and respect for re-entry intervals after spraying as stated on product labels. At seed units: protective equipment in treatment areas, awareness of forklifts and conveyors, and no entry into bins.

Evidence for assessment

EvidenceExample
Administrative recordsApplications you checked and captured, inspection schedules you prepared
Inspection reportsField and seed unit reports you completed
ReconciliationsFields to intake to lots to labels for a crop
Mentor testimonyObservation checklists and comments
Problem casesA rejected field or traceability gap and how it was resolved

Remove confidential client details from copies where required, keeping traceability for the assessor.

Key points

  • Check every field entry against listing, parent seed and cropping history.
  • Keep the certification register complete and reconcile it regularly.
  • Schedule inspections so no growth-stage window is missed.
  • Inspect fields and seed units against the scheme standards and record decisions.
  • Stay independent and declare conflicts of interest.
